Treated mice showed enhanced osteoblast differentiation, greater trabecular bone mass, and higher serum bone formation markers, with elevated urinary calcium but no sign of kidney stones and reduced serum creatinine. In immunodeficient and immunocompetent mice transplanted with 5TGM1 myeloma cells, treatment begun 4 weeks before transplantation prevented engraftment or substantially delayed myeloma growth, increased bone formation, raised osteoblast numbers, lowered osteoclast numbers, and prolonged survival; treatment begun after transplantation had smaller but significant effects. These findings identify this bioavailable, bone anabolic oral calcium as a candidate for preventing or delaying myeloma development and progression.

items.title: Enhancing the Efficacy of Oncolytic Viruses by Engineering Virus Host Interactions Using CRISPR Cas13d
items.abstract: Oncolytic herpes simplex virus type 1 (oHSV1) is a promising cancer therapy, but tumor cell antiviral responses can restrict viral replication. Strategies for temporally controlled targeting of antiviral factors remain limited. Here, we developed an inducible CRISPR Cas13d platform to modulate host responses during HSV1 infection. We screened 13 pharmacological inhibitors across tumor models to identify pathways associated with restricted infection. Reporter assays identified Cas13d as the preferred effector over Cas13b, while endogenous-target experiments demonstrated Cas13d mediated reductions in target protein abundance. We optimized guide RNA expression using RNA polymerase III promoters, selected p7SK, and established doxycycline-responsive Tet On and Tet Off systems. The platform was incorporated into HSV1 to generate a gRNA library targeting 15 host antiviral genes, together with two non-targeting controls. Doxycycline-dependent reporter readouts demonstrated inducible activity. Evaluation in EMT6, CT26, and 786 O cells revealed guide-dependent differences in fluorescence. These findings establish a programmable framework for investigating virus host interactions during oncolytic HSV infection.

items.title: Microbiome complexity shapes host transcriptional networks across the ileum-liver axis
items.abstract: The microbiome plays an increasingly recognised role in development, metabolism and immunity across all segments of the small and large intestine, as well as more distant organs such as the liver. In the terminal ileum - a key site of nutrient absorption - the presence of microbes dictates the development of secondary lymphoid structures (Peyers patches), mediates bile acid metabolism, and impacts absorption. In part, coordinated regulatory networks in the gut impact liver function and immunity through gut-liver connectivity and the movement of immune cells and bioactive small molecules that includes bile acids and other bacterial metabolites. We aimed to examine the extent of microbiome involvement in ileal transcription, where subtle changes in co-expression networks can be tuned by microbiome diversity, composition and function. We surveyed ileal transcriptomes across mouse models which vary in microbiome complexity ranging from germ-free (GF, n = 15), the Oligo-Mouse-Microbiota-12 (MM12, n = 15), and specific pathogen free (SPF, n = 15).

items.title: An atlas of the aging glycoproteome reveals how glycosylation modulates autoantibody binding in the brain
items.abstract: Protein N-glycosylation generates substantial molecular diversity, yet how glycan composition varies throughout aging remains poorly understood. We mapped the N-glycoproteome of brain, liver, spleen, kidney, and plasma across nine ages spanning the mouse lifespan, identifying 79,517 unique N-glycopeptides at 9,217 glycosites on 4,397 glycoproteins, with matched proteomic trajectories (glycoproteinatlas.org). Organ-specific differences were larger than age-related changes, but aging still remodeled numerous glycosites. Brain aging increased short paucimannose glycans, driven partly by increased abundance of hexosaminidase B (HEXB). In white matter, aging increased paucimannosylation of myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein (MOG), a major autoimmune target. We identified MOG-reactive autoantibodies in aged individuals and patients with MOG antibody-associated disease (MOGAD) and showed that MOG glycosylation modulates autoantibody binding. Glycosylation changes associated with normal aging were also observed after experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE), a model of autoimmune neuroinflammation. These findings reveal N-glycosylation as both a marker of age and a regulator of disease-relevant molecular interactions.

items.title: Chronic evoked seizures differentially worsen cognitive function and long-term neuropsychiatric comorbidities in Alzheimer's disease-related genotypes
items.abstract: Variants in one of three deterministic risk genes - amyloid precursor protein (APP), presenilin 1 (PSEN1), or presenilin 2 (PSEN2) - lead to early-onset Alzheimer's disease (EOAD), which also carries a high risk of spontaneous seizures. Seizures may worsen AD-related behavioral comorbidities, including depression, anxiety, and cognitive impairment. Using the corneal kindling model of secondarily generalized focal seizures in two distinct aged male and female EOAD-associated mouse models, we assessed the interaction between investigator-initiated chronic seizures and EOAD genotype on AD-related behavioral comorbidities. Genotypes were selected to model amyloid-b; independent and dependent AD risk factors and included: PSEN2-N141I (amyloid-b; independent model) versus wild-type (PSEN2 control) mice, and APP/PS1 (amyloid-b dependent model) versus wild-type littermates (Tg-). Sham and fully kindled mice then underwent behavioral assessment in the saccharin preference test of anhedonia-like behavior, the Barnes maze test of spatial learning and memory, and a 67-hour home cage monitoring of circadian activity. EOAD genotype only significantly affected kindling acquisition of aged APP/PS1 females. However, there was no significant genotype or kindling effect on saccharin preference, suggesting no adverse impact on anhedonia-like behavior. Cognitive performance in the Barnes maze was significantly worsened by seizures exclusively in APP/PS1 female mice. However, seizures generally worsened Barnes maze performance of male PSEN2-N141I and PSEN2 control mice. Finally, chronic seizures consistently worsened exploratory behavior patterns during home cage circadian activity monitoring exclusively in APP/PS1 male and female mice. This study reveals the AD-related heterogeneity of seizure-evoked behavioral consequences on spatial working memory and circadian behaviors.

items.title: Identification of a human Anxa1-associated dopaminergic population linked to Parkinson's disease vulnerability and sensorimotor putaminal networks
items.abstract: The selective loss of dopaminergic (DA) neurons drives motor symptoms of Parkinson's disease (PD). In mice, Anxa1+ SNc DA neurons are highly vulnerable in PD models, project to the dorsolateral striatum, and display movement-correlated activity, yet they lack clearly defined human counterparts. We transfer the mouse taxonomy to human using a hierarchical mixture-of-experts model, recovering a human Anxa1-associated population. We find that this was the most depleted subtype in PD brains. A ligand-receptor algorithm, validated against mouse tracing, infers that these neurons preferentially innervate the caudal putamen. There, DaT-SPECT shows the earliest and most severe DA axon loss in PD. Functional connectivity positions this region as a critical node within the somato-cognitive action network, linking DA neuron vulnerability to circuit dysfunction. To translate these insights, we present an interactive portal unifying human datasets with a cross-species FDA Drug Atlas, nominating CACNA1G as a candidate neuroprotective target for the Anxa1-associated population.

items.title: The language network responds stronger to connected than to unconnected sentences
items.corresponding_institution: Department of Diagnostic and Interventional Neuroradiology, University Medical Center Goettingen, Germany
items.abstract: Purpose: Reliable functional mapping of the language network and preoperative assessment of language lateralization are essential for safe and effective craniotomy in patients with lesions in language-eloquent brain regions, yet existing fMRI language paradigms are often time-consuming and place substantial cognitive and economic demands on patients and diagnostic services. Methods: We therefore tested ecologically valid German stimulus sets designed to optimize measurement efficiency. Forty-three healthy participants (mean age = 38 years, range = 20 - 64; 24 women) were scanned on a 3T MRI while reading or listening to 4-, 8-, and 12-word sentences and pseudoword lists or texts, each followed by a decision task. Sentences were selected from German literary classics and text passages from general-interest science magazines and matched across conditions for lexical and structural properties. Results: Region-of-interest analyses in subject-specific, functionally defined language-sensitive regions showed robust activation of the left-hemispheric language network across modalities. Within participants, texts elicited significantly larger effect sizes than sentences, and longer sentences generally produced stronger responses than shorter ones. Task manipulations expected to increase cognitive demand (short 4-word sentences with frequent probes, coherent texts requiring deeper semantic integration) did not enhance responses in the domain-general multiple demand network, indicating that executive-control activity did not overshadow language-selective activation, whereas substantial overlap between default mode and language-sensitive regions in the left temporal lobe was consistent with relatively automatic processing of connected language. Conclusions: These findings indicate that ecologically valid sentence- and text-based paradigms can provide efficient, language-specific fMRI protocols for preoperative diagnostics and individualized presurgical planning in patients with lesions near language-eloquent cortex.

items.title: Preparatory beta activity reflects the precision demands of an upcoming movement
items.abstract: Noise and external disturbances continuously push the limb away from its intended path, but not every deviation compromises the goal of an action. The accuracy constraints of a task define the range of acceptable endpoints and thereby set its precision demands, that is, how much noise must be attenuated for the task to succeed. Whether neural activity during movement preparation reflects these precision demands remains largely unexplored. We recorded electroencephalography (EEG) while healthy human participants (n = 27) prepared reaching movements toward narrow or wide targets at the same location and with the same timing constraints. An instructed delay before the go cue allowed preparatory activity to be isolated, and mechanical perturbations were applied during movement to probe feedback responses. Narrow targets led to more precise movements, with greater endpoint accuracy, lower variability and smaller perturbation-induced deviations. This was achieved without a reduction in movement speed, and involved greater muscle co-activation and larger long-latency responses to perturbations. Before movement onset, beta power (13-30 Hz) was lower for narrow than for wide targets, an effect that emerged late in the delay period and was concentrated over bilateral parieto-occipital electrodes. In contrast, alpha (8-12 Hz) and theta (4-7 Hz) activity did not differ between conditions. These findings demonstrate that preparatory beta activity is sensitive not only to kinematic requirements of the movement but also the precision with which it must be produced.

items.title: Intranasal oxytocin increases early tactile engagement with a robotic dog: A within-session effect without consolidation
items.abstract: Oxytocin (OXT) is centrally involved in mammalian affiliation, but whether it modulates affiliative behavior toward artificial social agents, and how such an effect unfolds within a single interaction, is unclear. In a randomized, double-blind, placebo (PLA)-controlled study, 61 healthy adult males received 40 IU intranasal OXT or PLA before interacting with a Sony aibo robotic dog across an initial free interaction, a cooperative task-learning phase, and a final free interaction, with ten affiliative behaviors coded from video. OXT increased tactile engagement early: participants touched aibo longer during the initial free interaction, the only outcome of ten to survive family-wise correction. A weaker increase in smile frequency did not survive correction, and instrumental behavior was unaffected. Contrary to our second prediction, the advantage was not consolidated: it held through the initial interaction, closed across the intervening task, and was absent at the final one. An exploratory decomposition located the effect: participants under OXT did not initiate contact more often, and the difference was carried by how long each episode of contact was sustained. Urinary OXT confirmed group-level exposure. Because the design included no comparison condition and confounded interaction period with elapsed time and pharmacokinetics, it cannot establish bond formation, robot specificity, or consolidation as a psychological process. What it does bound is where and when OXT acted: on the maintenance of contact rather than its initiation, and only while the agent was novel, a pattern that fits salience- and novelty-based accounts better than bond formation.

items.title: Reduced subcortical envelope phase locking in middle age without detectable changes in perceptual discrimination
items.corresponding_institution: STMS Lab (CNRS / Ircam / Sorbonne Universite, Ministere de la Culture), 1 place Igor Stravinsky, 75004 Paris, France
items.abstract: Cochlear synaptopathy (CS) can occur during normal aging without elevated audiometric thresholds and has been hypothesized to contribute to suprathreshold auditory difficulties. Frequency-following responses (FFRs) have been proposed as markers of CS, but whether their envelope- and temporal-fine-structure-related components are similarly affected by age, and whether such changes relate to perceptual sensitivity, remains unclear. Here, we examined associations between age-related FFR changes and perceptual sensitivity in young (n = 20, 19-32 years) and middle-aged (n = 20, 40-58 years) adults with clinically normal hearing. Participants completed psychoacoustic discrimination tasks for formant frequency, formant bandwidth, and temporal-envelope shape using stationary stimuli in quiet and background noise. FFRs were recorded using dynamic stimuli varying along the same acoustic dimensions. We quantified envelope- and temporal-fine-structure-related phase locking (PLVENV and PLVTFS) across harmonics and assessed how it tracked stimulus changes over time. Mean PLVENV decreased significantly with age, and PLVENV tracking of decreasing formant bandwidth and temporal-envelope shape weakened with age. In contrast, mean PLVTFS and temporal slopes of PLVTFS spectral centroid were not significantly associated with age. Discrimination thresholds showed no significant associations with age, either in quiet or in noise, and PLV measures did not significantly explain individual differences in discrimination thresholds. These findings indicate that age-related reductions in subcortical envelope phase locking can be detected by middle age without corresponding measurable reductions in perceptual sensitivity.

items.title: Terminally differentiated CX3CR1+ natural killer cells drive coronary arteritis through an NFAT-T-bet axis
items.abstract: Natural killer (NK) cells acquire potent effector function through terminal differentiation, yet the signals driving this program toward pathogenicity in vascular inflammation remain undefined. Using an FK565-induced mouse model of Kawasaki disease and single-cell transcriptomics from patients, we identify NK cells as major drivers of coronary arteritis through cytotoxicity and CCL5-CCR1-mediated recruitment of myeloid cells. This activity is concentrated in a terminally differentiated, T-bet-driven NK cell subset, the cardiac accumulation of which depends on CX3CR1, and a corresponding population is enriched in patient transcriptomic datasets. We further identify signaling through calcineurin and nuclear factor of activated T cells (NFAT) as an upstream driver of this program, with NFATc1 induced in NK cells. Calcineurin inhibition suppressed T-bet induction, reduced this subset and attenuated disease development. These findings define an NFAT-T-bet-CX3CR1 axis that couples terminal NK cell differentiation to coronary inflammation.

items.title: Dynamic T-cell receptor repertoire remodeling is associated with murine and human lung allograft dysfunction
items.corresponding_institution: Department of Medicine, David Geffen School of Medicine, University of California, Los Angeles, Los Angeles, California, United States of America
items.abstract: Chronic lung allograft dysfunction (CLAD) is a major cause of late graft failure after lung transplantation. Acute cellular rejection is an established risk factor for CLAD. However, its diagnosis by biopsy may incompletely capture dynamic and spatially heterogeneous immune remodeling within the allograft. We investigated whether lung graft proximal T-cell receptor beta-chain (TCR{beta}) repertoire features reflect alloimmune remodeling and associate with acute cellular rejection (ACR) and CLAD. TCR{beta}; sequencing was performed on graft-infiltrating T-cells from a murine orthotopic lung transplant model and on 90 longitudinal bronchoalveolar lavage cell-pellet (BAL-cp) samples from 23 lung transplant recipients during the first post-transplant year. In the murine model, allografts showed persistent histologic injury and strong, consistent TCR{beta}; repertoire remodeling relative to isografts. Across days 28 and 56, murine allografts had higher productive clonality (Cliff's {delta}; = 0.93, p = 0.0087) and maximum productive frequency (Cliff's {delta}; = 0.93, p = 0.014), with complete rank separation at each time point. Murine allografts also exhibited greater pairwise Morisita repertoire overlap (p < 0.0001) and enrichment of recurrent, high-frequency shared clonotypes. Productive clonality from human lung transplant recipients' BAL-cp was higher at the a priori selected month-6 visit from patients who developed CLAD, as compared to those who remained CLAD-free (p = 0.0326). In a month-6 surveillance-visit index analysis, high productive clonality was associated with early onset CLAD (CLAD within 2 years of transplant) (log-rank p = 0.038). In a patient-specific index-event analysis, CLAD-free survival differed across high and low productive clonality groups among acute rejectors (log-rank p = 0.019). Together, these findings establish measurable graft-localized TCR{beta}; repertoire remodeling and position BAL TCR{beta}; profiling as a potential complement to biopsy diagnosis. With validation in larger cohorts, graft-proximal repertoire measures may help identify CLAD-associated immune states before the onset of lung function decline and inform more individualized surveillance.

items.title: A Conserved Interface Between COG4 and Syntaxin 5 Is Essential for Intra-Golgi Membrane Trafficking
items.corresponding_institution: Department of Physiology and Cell Biology, University of Arkansas for Medical Sciences, Little Rock. AR, 72205, USA
items.abstract: The conserved oligomeric Golgi (COG) complex tethers retrograde intra-Golgi transport vesicles, but how it engages the SNARE machinery to support vesicle fusion remains unclear. Here, we identify a functional interface between the COG subunit COG4 and the Qa-SNARE Syntaxin 5 (STX5). The C-terminal region of COG4 coprecipitated with STX5, and AlphaFold3 modeling placed the COG4 MUN-C-like subdomain in contact with the STX5 Ha-Hb loop and the linker connecting its Habc domain to the SNARE motif. Replacing the Ha-Hb loop with a flexible Gly/Ser sequence preserved STX5 localization and its interaction with SCFD1 but impaired rescue of GPP130 abundance and protein glycosylation in STX5-depleted cells. Combining the loop replacement with linker substitutions reduced recovery of COG3 and the SNARE partner GS15 with STX5 and led to vesicle accumulation around disorganized Golgi cisternae. On the COG4 side of the interface with Qa-SNARE, alanine substitution of the conserved residues D452 and D453 reduced coprecipitation with STX5. Replacing these residues with either alanine or lysine preserved COG4 localization and COG8 recruitment to the Golgi but failed to restore normal glycosylation, GS15 localization, or altered Golgi morphology in COG4-knockout cells. These findings support a model in which the COG4-STX5 interface couples vesicle tethering to productive SNARE assembly, thereby controlling vesicular retrograde trafficking and Golgi organization.

items.title: Physical constraints on the social-genetic dynamics of mtDNA inside plant mitochondria
items.abstract: Mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) encodes essential cellular machinery and is contained within mitochondria. This physical containment shapes the genetic dynamics of mtDNA populations in the cell. In plants (and other non-bilaterians), mtDNA colocalisation is essential for recombination, while other cellular priorities may favour mtDNA spacing through the cell. Given possible physical interactions between mtDNA and the inner mitochondrial membrane and its cristae, it is not clear how readily or often this colocalisation may occur. Only limited, indirect evidence exists supporting the capacity for plant mtDNAs to physically colocalise. Here, we survey evidence from recent and new single-cell timelapse microscopy to quantitatively characterise the motion of mtDNA nucleoids inside vegetative plant cells. We combine biophysical arguments with new microscopy data and spatial statistics to demonstrate the subdiffusive but not internally static nature of nucleoids, demonstrating that they are enriched at the termini of elongated mitochondria and well-spaced through the cell but capable of colocalisation. We also describe other modes of physical motion that may impact the genetic dynamics of mtDNA populations, and discuss the implication of this physical behaviour for cytoplasmic genetics.

items.title: Non-invasive detection of tissue clonal mosaicism in chronic disease
items.corresponding_institution: New York Genome Center, New York, NY, USA; Department of Systems and Computational Biomedicine, Weill Cornell Medicine, New York, NY, USA.
items.abstract: Liquid biopsy has transformed our ability to non-invasively interrogate the somatic genome, but its reach has been largely confined to fetal genetics in prenatal testing and tumor genetics in cancer. Clonal mosaicism (CM) pervades non-malignant solid tissues, where somatic driver mutations expand under specific selective pressures and may shape the course of chronic illness. Access to this biology has been limited to invasive tissue biopsies, restricting the field to small cohorts and single time points, and has precluded large-scale, clinically-linked analyses. Here, ultra-sensitive cell-free DNA (cfDNA) sequencing of patients with chronic liver disease revealed genome-wide somatic variants from matched liver biopsies at plasma fractions comparable to those of cancers (10^-4 - 10^-5), with signal corresponding to variants from spatially and phylogenetically related clones. A biopsy-naive targeted panel detected pathogenic variants in chronic liver disease driver genes in 81.5% patients with chronic liver disease, undetectable in controls, with stage-specific enrichment of ACVR2A in early disease and clearance of liver-derived signal following transplant. Extending the framework to inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), we detect clonal expansions of IBD driver genes in active ulcerative colitis, and observe greater detection in patients with pancolitis versus more localized disease. Together, these results open a new domain for cfDNA genetics beyond cancer and prenatal genetics, the non-invasive interrogation of somatic evolution in chronic disease, and establish a framework for the large-cohort, longitudinal, clinically linked studies of solid-tissue CM that has been inaccessible to the field.

items.title: Genomics of the diversification of Heliconius cydno (Lepidoptera: Nymphalidae) in northern South America: geographic and phenotypic patterns
items.corresponding_institution: School of Sciences and Engineering, Biology Program, Universidad del Rosario, Bogota D.C., Colombia
items.abstract: The interplay between natural selection, gene flow, and geography is a key driver of population differentiation. This study investigates their influence on the recent adaptive radiation of Heliconius cydno, a mimetic and aposematic butterfly with striking variation in wing color pattern across its distribution in Central and northern South America. The genetic basis of this phenotypic diversity has a modular architecture, whereby a few key genes and cis-regulatory elements control differences among morphotypes. Using whole-genome sequences from 133 individuals representing all subspecies of H. cydno, we investigated (1) the role of Andean orogeny in its diversification and (2) the genetic basis of the variation in the hindwing white submarginal band, which to date, had remained unknown. First, we found that five of the fourteen described subspecies correspond to distinct monophyletic lineages and well-defined genetic clusters that originated in northwestern South America and later expanded into Central America and the Colombian inter-Andean valleys. Second, we observed signatures of genetic structure that were consistent with geographic patterns, particularly those associated with the inter-Andean region and Gorgona Island. Third, we identified ivory:mir-193 as the locus underlying variation in the white submarginal band on the hindwing. We also detected evidence of introgression suggesting that this trait was likely transferred from H. cydno to H. melpomene, contributing to the establishment of a novel mimicry ring with H. erato. Altogether, these findings highlight the roles of geography, genomic architecture, and introgression in the diversification of H. cydno.

items.title: The Impact of Germ Layer Origin on the Ageing Transcriptome
items.abstract: Ageing is accompanied by widespread changes in gene expression, yet whether these changes share any common organisation across groups of tissues remains unclear. Adult tissues arise from three embryonic germ layers (ectoderm, mesoderm and endoderm), so shared developmental lineage could influence how tissues age. Using bulk RNA-seq data from 24 GTEx tissues, we estimated age effects in each tissue with limma-voom and combined them within each germ layer by random-effects meta-analysis. Endoderm had the most significant age-associated genes (4,805), followed by mesoderm (4,520) and ectoderm (1,744), but this order reversed for genes with consistent effects across tissues of the same germ layer. These consistent genes were largely germ layer specific, although mesoderm and endoderm shared more than expected by chance. Ageing profiles were significantly more similar between tissues from the same germ layer than between tissues from different germ layers. Germ layer origin also explained 13.6% of the variation in tissue ageing profiles. Co-expression networks of ageing were organised differently in each germ layer, and 43% of enriched biological processes were specific to one germ layer. However, after grouping related processes, most functional themes were shared by all three, and genes shared between modules of different germ layers were enriched mainly for immune processes. Together, these results indicate that germ layer origin leaves a small but detectable imprint on transcriptomic ageing. However, tissue-specific and shared immune programmes are also prominent.

items.title: Machine Learning-based Transcriptomic Data Analysis of Long COVID Patients: Generating Hypotheses for Molecular Signatures
items.abstract: Introduction: Long COVID (LC) remains a global public-health challenge, affecting an estimated 10-30% of COVID-19-survivors. Machine learning (ML) can help identify molecular features associated with LC. Human ion channels (HICs), that regulate immune-cell signaling and cellular homeostasis, may contribute to LC-associated processes and offer insights into relevant pathways and potential drug-repurposing candidates. Methodology: RNA-seq data from COVID-19-recovered and LC patients across six datasets were integrated, preprocessed, and corrected for batch effects. Supervised ML models were evaluated using leave-one-batch-out validation, with SHAP identifying features across validation folds. Functional enrichment, host-host and host-viral protein-protein interaction analyses were performed, followed by drug interaction analysis of potential HICs within the resulting interactome. Results: A support vector classifier with an RBF kernel achieved a mean-AUC of 0.664 across six validation folds. SHAP analysis of the three selected folds (AUC = 0.722, 0.836, and 0.817) identified 225, 153, and 241 genes, respectively. Functional enrichment highlighted pathways including histidine metabolism and TNF signaling. Among the 613 genes identified across these folds, 9 were HICs and 39 were immune signaling-related genes (ISGs), whose protein-protein interaction analysis revealed a pharmacologically relevant interactome. Furthermore, four HICs including CLCN3, KCNQ3, RYR1, and ZACN interacted with 30 approved drugs. Conclusion: ML-based analysis of integrated RNA-seq data identified HICs and ISGs associated with LC, while functional enrichment and PPI analyses provided insights into their potential biological relevance. Drug interaction analysis further highlighted candidate HIC-targeting drugs for future investigation in LC management. This computational framework provides preliminary, hypothesis-generating insights to guide future research.

items.title: NanoHIV-DR: a Nextflow workflow for consensus and read level HIV-1 drug resistance profiling from Oxford Nanopore sequencing
items.corresponding_institution: London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine
items.abstract: Oxford Nanopore sequencing offers a rapid and portable approach for HIV-1 drug resistance (HIVDR) genotyping, but analysis of the resulting long-read data requires multiple bioinformatics steps and currently available nanopore workflows are limited. We developed NanoHIV-DR, a Nextflow-based workflow that streamlines the analysis of Oxford Nanopore sequencing data and generation of HIVDR reports. NanoHIV-DR processes raw POD5 files through basecalling, demultiplexing, host-read removal, quality filtering, read alignment and consensus generation, before identifying resistance-associated mutations and interpreting predicted drug susceptibility. The workflow provides two complementary approaches to HIVDR analysis: consensus-based resistance interpretation using Sierra and read-level detection of resistance-associated variants, enabling mutations below the consensus level to be identified and quantified. Outputs are integrated with clinical metadata to generate human-readable HIVDR reports. NanoHIV-DR provides a reproducible and accessible workflow for Nanopore-based HIVDR analysis with reduced bioinformatics expertise and manual processing for translating long-read sequencing data into interpretable resistance profiles.

items.title: Machine learning prediction of antimicrobial resistance in respiratory metagenomes
items.abstract: Background: Targeted therapy for patients with suspected respiratory infections traditionally requires bacterial culture followed by phenotypic antimicrobial susceptibility testing (AST), a process that can take up to 5 days. In acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), delays in identifying the causative pathogen and its resistance profile may be especially harmful because patients are critically ill and often receive broad-spectrum empiric antibiotics. The growing burden of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) further complicates clinical decision-making by reducing effective treatment options and increasing the risk of inadequate initial therapy. Culture-free, AI-driven computational metagenomic strategies have the potential to drastically shorten this window, enabling more rapid targeted therapy prescription. To show the feasibility of such approaches, we develop a proof-of-concept framework based on clinical metagenomics. Methods: We simulated respiratory metagenomes using real-world bacterial genomes with associated antimicrobial susceptibility phenotypes. Each simulated metagenome contained a fixed commensal background and one clinically important respiratory pathogen, Acinetobacter baumannii, Klebsiella pneumoniae, or Pseudomonas aeruginosa, at 5% or 10% bacterial read abundance. Realistic reads were simulated for Oxford Nanopore, PacBio, and Illumina sequencing platforms. Random Forest (RF) classifiers were trained and evaluated using five-fold, strain-grouped cross-validation with fold-specific {chi}2-ranked 13-mer features. ResFinder and KARGA were included as reference-based metagenomics benchmarks and evaluated using the same five held-out folds across the three sequencing platforms and two pathogen-abundance conditions. Results: RF performance varied substantially across species, antibiotics, and sequencing platforms. The strongest and most consistent results were observed for K. pneumoniae, with accuracy reaching approximately 0.96 for ceftazidime, 0.93 for amikacin, and 0.92 for ciprofloxacin. Performance for P. aeruginosa was more heterogeneous: long-read models performed well for amikacin, reaching 0.89 with PacBio and 0.88 with Nanopore, whereas Illumina performed substantially better for ciprofloxacin, ceftazidime, and levofloxacin, reaching accuracies of approximately 0.87, 0.77, and 0.70, respectively. Across most organism-antibiotic combinations, RF accuracy was numerically higher than the classification accuracies obtained with KARGA and ResFinder, which generally remained near 0.50. Increasing pathogen abundance from 5% to 10% and increasing the number of selected features from 2,500 to 5,000 generally produced modest improvements in classification accuracy, although the magnitude of improvement varied across organism-antibiotic combinations and sequencing platforms. Conclusions: Genome-wide k-mer machine learning can recover phenotype-associated antimicrobial resistance signals from simulated respiratory metagenomes, although performance depends strongly on the organism, antibiotic, and sequencing platform. These results represent a simulation-based proof of concept.

items.title: Predicted templates improve the prediction of antibody-antigen structures by AlphaFold 3 and Boltz-2
items.abstract: Motivation: In spite of the much improved protein structure prediction methods, the success rate remains low for antibody-antigen complexes. While this can be improved by computationally demanding massive sampling, results are still much poorer than for most other types of protein-protein interactions. In principle, improvement can be achieved by using templates that are close enough to the native structure of the complex, but these are generally not available for antibody-antigen complexes. Results: We explore the use of templates, generated by the computationally inexpensive rigid body docking program PIPER. Applied to a leakage-free antibody-antigen benchmark set, standard AlphaFold 3 with 1000 random seeds yields acceptable or better models as the top predictions for 56.2% of complexes. Adding the PIPER generated templates in the unmasked version of AlphaFold 3 either increases the success rate to 63.4%, or reaches the same 56.2% success rate in about 200 runs. The template-based approach similarly improves antibody-antigen prediction by Boltz-2. This result demonstrates that the space explored by the ML based approach can be expanded by adding templates prepared by traditional docking, compensating for the lack of evolutionary relationship and the limited availability of training data. Availability and Implementation: The ClusPro server (https://cluspro.bu.edu/login.php) containing the PIPER program is free for non-commercial applications and the program is available by request (https://www.vajdalab.org/). All other study data are included in the article and/or supporting information.

items.title: Large populations from few founders: founder-aware likelihoods for inferring cell proliferation rates
items.abstract: Gaussian approximations to demographic noise are usually justified by large numbers of cells. In populations described by branching processes, however, a large population descended from few founders is not approximately Gaussian. A culture grown from few cells can contain thousands of cells yet retain large, skewed variation from its earliest divisions, deaths, and phenotypic switches. A random establishment amplitude, the limit of the population size divided by its exponential growth factor, summarizes this variation. We propose a founder-aware likelihood for cell cultures observed at an endpoint. Given the establishment amplitude, it approximates the remaining demographic fluctuations by a Gaussian distribution and then averages over the distribution of the amplitude. Its conditional Gaussian approximation requires a large population rather than many founders, and the likelihood approaches a single Gaussian distribution as the founder count grows. We compare it with a population Gaussian likelihood developed for many-founder cultures, using a pure-birth (Yule) process, whose cell-count distribution is known exactly, and exact simulations of a two-type process with division, death, and reversible switching. With one founder per culture, the founder-aware likelihood estimates rates more accurately than the population Gaussian likelihood, and its confidence sets are longer but have coverage close to the nominal level. With 50 founders per culture, the two likelihoods perform comparably. Founder-aware likelihoods thus suit clonal and other few-founder experiments.

items.title: Investigating Motor Skill Acquisition in Mice and Humans: Towards A Cross-Species Paradigm
items.corresponding_institution: Max Planck Institute for Human Development
items.abstract: Relating non-invasive observations of human brain plasticity to cellular processes identified in animal models remains a major challenge in neuroscience. We address this challenge by introducing a paradigm for studying motor skill acquisition across species. We designed a human chopstick grasping task modeled after the rodent single-pellet reaching task, resulting in a comparable sequence of reach-to-grasp movements across species. We studied 48 young adult male C57BL/6N mice and 71 young men, comparing trained groups with untrained controls. In both mice and humans, structural magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) was performed before, during, and after motor training. The functional form of behavioral performance gains on the trained task was highly similar across species. In trained compared to control mice, analysis of the early learning interval revealed decreases in regional volume in contralateral primary motor and forelimb somatosensory cortices, with greater volume reductions in primary motor cortex associated with better reaching performance. In humans, performance gains transferred to other chopstick tasks but not to general dexterity, and no reliable changes in gray matter volume were observed. Quantitative MRI, however, revealed early training-related changes in tissue-sensitive measures, including increases in magnetization transfer saturation (MTsat) and longitudinal relaxation rate (R1) in contralateral motor and frontal regions, potentially reflecting an increase in intracortical myelin. Thus, early structural changes in the contralateral motor cortex were detected in both species, but the degree to which these changes reflect a common biological mechanism is unclear. We conclude that the present cross-species paradigm provides a viable starting point for studying brain plasticity across species. Future work needs to relate macroscopic structural changes more directly to cellular processes by applying longitudinal microscopic imaging and MRI in the same animals.

items.title: Perineuronal net homeostasis by the NRG1/ErbB4 signaling for cognitive function
items.corresponding_institution: Chinese Institutes for Medical Research, Beijing
items.abstract: Perineuronal nets (PNN) is the specialized extracellular matrix that enwraps the soma and proximal dendrites of neurons in particular interneurons. During neural development, PNN expression marks the closure of the critical period of visual cortical development. The roles of PNN in the adult brain and how its expression is regulated remain less understood. Here we show that enriched environment (EE) increases PNN in the prefrontal cortex (PFC) in adult mice with improved cognitive functions. Analysis of snRNA-seq data of EE and control PFC identified the neuregulin1 (NRG1)/ErbB4 signaling as the pathway to regulate PNN expression. Ablation of ErbB4 or acute chemical genetic inhibition of its kinase activity reduced PNN and impaired cognitive function and prevented the promotion effect of EE. The expression of PNN and the core component aggrecan (ACAN) was increased in cultured interneurons stimulated with NRG1. ACAN mutation abolished PNN, weakened excitatory inputs and intrinsic excitability of ErbB4+ interneurons, and impaired cognitive functions. ACAN could undergo liquid-liquid phase separation to form condensates alone or together with other proteoglycans of the PNN. Finally, we demonstrate that restoring ACAN could ameliorate PNN and cognitive deficits in ErbB4 mutant mice. These results suggest that EE may improve cognitive functions by enhancing NRG1/ErbB4 signaling to increase PNN levels, identifying a signaling pathway critical to PNN homeostasis in adult animals

items.title: Mechanical strain and strain rate define thresholds of single-cell and ensemble calcium disruption in traumatic brain injury
items.abstract: Mechanically induced brain injury triggers rapid cellular responses that shape long-term neurological outcomes, yet the early evolution of functional network disruption remains poorly defined. In particular, how neuronal activity changes within seconds of deformation and whether these responses determine subsequent circuit organization remain unknown. Here, we combined controlled mechanical stretch with high-speed calcium imaging to measure neuronal calcium dynamics within seconds of injury and track the same cells over 24 hours. We identify strain- and strain-rate-dependent disruption modes, including rapid reduction of calcium transient activity under moderate loading and collapse of network bursting beyond distinct mechanical thresholds. These disruptions persist despite preserved cell viability, revealing an additional functional injury pathway. These findings show that functional impairment emerges within seconds of mechanical loading and that the severity of deformation dictates the mode of network disruption, establishing mechanical thresholds as key determinants of secondary injury progression.

items.title: Modulation of genetic- and toxicant-induced Parkinson's disease outcomes by SV2C in C. elegans
items.abstract: Several proteins involved in dopaminergic neurotransmission have been implicated in Parkinson's disease (PD), including synaptic vesicle glycoprotein 2C (SV2C). At least seven SNPs in SV2C are associated with PD, including variants that modify: PD risk, PD risk in GBA carriers, PD severity, contribution of environmental factors (e.g., nicotine) to PD, and PD patient response to L-DOPA and dopamine therapies. Although the specific function of SV2C remains unknown, there is significant evidence supporting a role of SV2C in mediating vesicular dopamine content, vesicular trafficking, and neurotransmitter release. Furthermore, SV2C directly associates with -synuclein and mediates the content of neurotoxicants within synaptic vesicles. Taken together, these data suggest that SV2C plays a critical role in mediating PD risk and pathogenesis. To investigate whether SV2C mediates PD outcomes, transgenic Caenorhabditis elegans (C. elegans) expressing human SV2C, human -synuclein, or both, were exposed to the PD-associated neurotoxicants 1-methyl-4-phenylpyridinium (MPP+), rotenone, and paraquat, and evaluated for PD outcomes including lethality and dopamine-mediated motor behavior. Although SV2C-expressing C. elegans showed a shorter lifespan at baseline, SV2C expression conferred organism-level protection against MPP+ and paraquat-induced lethality. While -synuclein expression exacerbated lethality following MPP+ and paraquat exposure, SV2C provided partial rescue of lethality in -synuclein-expressing C. elegans. However, no differences in lethality were observed based on genotype following rotenone exposure. Interestingly, sublethal toxicant exposure did not reveal a protective effect of SV2C expression on motor behavior for any of the toxicants. To determine whether SV2C's modulation of vesicular uptake mediated the protection against lethality from PD-associated neurotoxicants observed in C. elegans, in vitro assays of vesicular dopamine uptake dynamics were performed. SV2C expression resulted in a protective shift in toxicant-induced uptake inhibition following MPP+ and rotenone exposure; however, there was no paraquat-induced inhibition of vesicular uptake observed in vitro. Taken together, these data suggest that while SV2C plays a protective role in mediating organism-level survival in C. elegans following MPP+ and paraquat exposure, the mechanisms of protection and the role of SV2C in modulating vesicular dopamine dynamics and dopamine-mediated behaviors following toxicant exposure require further analysis. Future studies can evaluate additional PD outcomes in these exposure models and investigate SV2C-mediated mechanisms of protection such as regulation of neurotransmitter handling and oxidative stress.

items.title: Cross-domain competition for memory reactivation resources during sleep
items.abstract: Targeted Memory Reactivation (TMR) enhances the consolidation of both declarative and procedural memories. As previous research highlights the importance of cross-domain interactions in shaping memory consolidation, we investigated here whether interacting memories from different domains can be co-reactivated by TMR during post-learning sleep, and in turn enhance consolidation. In a fully within-subject design, twenty-four young, healthy participants learned both a motor and an object sequence learning task that were linked or not by a shared ordinal structure. TMR cues associated only with the object task were presented during post-learning non-rapid eye movement (NREM) sleep which was monitored with electroencephalography (EEG) during a 90-minute nap. We tested whether reactivating object memories would indirectly reactivate the linked motor memory. Behavioral results showed no overall effect of association but indicated that TMR disrupted object memory consolidation without indirectly affecting performance on the linked motor task. Sleep EEG data point to a competition for reactivation resources whereby slow oscillation (SO; 0.5-2 Hz) and spindle activity (12-16 Hz) involved in both memory protection and potentiation during sleep were preferentially allocated to the covert consolidation of the motor trace at the expense of object memory. These findings suggest that cross-domain memories sharing a common learning structure compete for consolidation resources during post-learning sleep.

items.title: Shared Neural Dynamics of Sentence-Level Language Processing in Verbally Proficient Autistic and Non-Autistic Adults
items.abstract: Autistic individuals often show atypical language development during childhood, yet many attain typical language proficiency by adulthood. This raises the question of whether the neural processes supporting language differ in autism once language has been acquired. Using electroencephalography (EEG), we compared verbally proficient autistic and non-autistic adults during rapid serial visual presentation of structured sentences and pseudoword lists. Sentence processing elicited oscillatory responses across theta, alpha, beta, and gamma frequency bands, with distinct spatiotemporal profiles and hemispheric lateralization most pronounced in the theta, alpha, and beta bands. Notably, beta-band activity increased over sentence position and was positively associated with verbal ability, consistent with a role in the maintenance and integration of linguistic information. These effects were highly comparable across groups, with similar patterns observed at both the individual and group levels and across sensor- and source-level analyses. Together, these findings indicate largely shared neural dynamics of sentence-level language processing in verbally proficient autistic and non-autistic adults, suggesting that atypical language-related neural organization is not an inevitable feature of autism in adulthood.

items.title: Distinct effects of aging and hearing loss on mouse auditory cortex
items.abstract: Age-related hearing loss is accompanied by changes in auditory cortical activity, but it remains unclear which changes reflect aging itself and which depend on the loss of peripheral input. Here we compared spontaneous and sound-evoked activity in the auditory cortex of awake C57BL/6J (C57) mice, which develop early-onset hearing loss, with that of C57BL/6J x CBA/Ca F1 hybrid mice, which retain their hearing. In both strains, aging increased the irregularity of spontaneous firing and reduced the spike-timing precision of narrow-spiking neurons during natural sound presentation. In C57 mice, aging was additionally associated with a greater loss of sound-responsive neurons, increased spontaneous firing of broad-spiking neurons and more variable sound-evoked spike trains. At the level of individual neurons, the effect of sound on contrast entropy, a firing-rate-normalized measure of spike-pattern diversity, also diverged between strains with age and became negative in middle-aged and old C57's neurons. Nevertheless, population activity discriminated spontaneous, natural sound-evoked and noise-evoked conditions with high accuracy at every age in both strains. Thus, aging and hearing loss have distinct effects on the spiking of individual auditory cortical neurons, whereas population activity continues to discriminate sound conditions.

items.title: Modular innate recognition in conventional T cells through FcRγ reconstitution
items.abstract: Engineered T cells can elicit durable tumor responses but largely rely on TCRs or CARs for target recognition. Here we show that FcR{gamma}, an innate signaling adaptor not expressed by conventional T cells, enables full-length innate receptor function in adult human {beta} T cells. FcR{gamma} reconstitution enabled endogenous NKp30 surface expression and cytotoxicity without inducing an innate-like state. Stable co-expression of NKp30 and FcR{gamma} maintained receptor expression after activation withdrawal, supported sustained tumor killing, delayed leukemia progression in mice, and enabled cytotoxicity against primary myeloid leukemia. FcR{gamma} also supported functional import of receptors spanning natural cytotoxicity, Fc receptor, and C-type lectin families, extending conventional T cell responses to tumor ligands, antibody-coated targets, IgE receptor engagement, and microbial patterns. These findings establish a shared-adaptor strategy for expanding innate recognition in engineered T cells while preserving the identity and functional properties of the widely adopted conventional T cell platform.

items.title: Structural analysis of DNA binding and flexibility of the homohexameric AAA+ helicase SaPIbov1 Rep
items.abstract: The replication initiation proteins (Reps) encoded by Staphylococcus aureus pathogenicity islands (SaPIs) are helicases that recognize their own origins of replication (oris). Despite their ability to melt the cognate ori without accessory proteins, the nature of the transition from origin-loaded to actively unwinding states remains poorly understood. Here, we report crystal and cryo-EM structures of the SaPIbov1 Rep, a homohexameric superfamily 6 (SF6) helicase, in apo and nucleotide plus duplex DNA-bound states. Comparison to superfamily 3 (SF3) SaPI Reps and archaeal/eukaryotic MCMs reveals differing structural adaptations for DNA engagement. Notably, SaPIbov1 Rep retains pore-loop 1 (PL1) and the pre-sensor 1 {beta}-hairpin (PS1) for DNA-binding, but lacks the Helix-2 insertion (H2i) conserved in MCM helicases and instead possesses an elongated PS1 providing extended DNA contact. 3D variability analysis (3DVA) resolved multiple ring-open conformational intermediate states, with ring asymmetry correlating to DNA binding. The duplex-bound single hexamer captured here likely represents a pre-replicative intermediate preceding double hexamer assembly. We also show that the disordered N-terminus of SaPIbov1 Rep binds its cognate primase and predict that the primase recruits the host DNA polymerase III.

items.title: TXNDC17 and glutathione cooperate to prevent cystine-induced cell death
items.corresponding_institution: Rudolf Virchow Zentrum (RVZ), Center for Integrative and Translational Bioimaging, University of Wuerzburg, Wuerzburg, Germany.
items.abstract: Glutathione (GSH) supports diverse metabolic and antioxidant functions, yet the cellular processes most vulnerable to its depletion remain incompletely defined. Using genome-wide genetic screening in GSH depleted cells, we identified the cystine reductase TXNDC17 as essential for survival under GSH limitation. GSH depletion in TXNDC17-knockout cells caused intracellular cystine accumulation, increased protein cysteinylation, and cell death. Inhibiting the cystine/glutamate antiporter system xC- prevented cell death, linking this vulnerability to cystine uptake and impaired intracellular reduction. GSH depletion also markedly suppressed the growth of xenografts derived from TXNDC17-knockout, KEAP1-mutant lung cancer cells with high system xC- activity, accompanied by reduction-sensitive changes in cytoskeletal proteins. We further identified an electrophilic fragment that induced dose-dependent cytotoxicity in GSH-depleted cancer cells in a cystine-uptake dependent manner. Together, our findings establish TXNDC17 and GSH as central regulators of cystine-driven cytotoxicity, uncovering a therapeutic vulnerability in cancers with high cystine uptake.

items.title: First Broad-spectrum Sami and Norse diets in northern Norway over the last 4000 years revealed by sedaDNA
items.corresponding_institution: The Arctic University Museum of Norway, UiT-The Arctic University of Norway
items.abstract: The comprehensive specification of palaeo-diets has depended upon the preservation of plants and bones in archaeological deposits, which is limited by preservation conditions. Although middens at settlement sites in northern Norway can have comprehensive faunal archives they still may not reflect the full diet. Here, we apply sedaDNA metabarcoding and shotgun sequencing to two midden complexes in Finnmark, Norway. At both sites, this doubled the species identified. At the Bankgohppi "Gressbakken" house site (c.4.5-3.8 BP), items were added to all food categories (Figure below) including mammals such as reindeer, beaver, and bowhead whale, suggesting deep-sea fishing practice. At the Finnes coastal Sami Early Metal Age site (c.07-0.8 BP) and later Norse Medieval re-occupation, sedaDNA added terrestrial mammal (reindeer) and domesticated stock (goat, cattle) to the diet. The combination of traditional data with sedaDNA data provides us for the first time with a broad spectrum, suggesting seasonally balanced diets and fishing activity in northern Norway over the last 4000 years.

items.title: Reproductive competition amplifies purifying selection and reduces genetic load
items.abstract: Deleterious mutations impose genetic load, and purging them through hard selection can carry substantial demographic costs. Competitive and sexual selection can instead remove deleterious variation through differential reproductive success. What remains unclear is when this process is more efficient than equivalent hard selection, and how competition generates this advantage. Here, we use forward-time simulations to express the impact of competition as an effective selection coefficient (se) calibrated against hard selection. Competition with multiple rivals strongly amplified purifying selection, whereas repeated contests improved discrimination by averaging stochastic and environmental variation. Strong competition also reduced genetic load relative to hard selection. These effects can shift weakly deleterious mutations from drift-dominated behaviour towards efficient purging. By front-loading purifying selection into reproduction, competitive selection can reduce genetic load at lower demographic cost. This provides a population-genetic mechanism by which genic capture can translate genome-wide genetic quality into more effective purifying selection. This may be particularly important in bottlenecked populations, where demographic recovery can relax purifying selection and allow genomic erosion to persist.

items.title: Evolutionary constraints on mitochondrial bioenergetics are reshaped in cancer
items.abstract: Mitochondrial DNA encodes thirteen subunits of the oxidative phosphorylation system, many of which are subject to strong purifying selection in humans. In cancer this selection is relaxed, which is usually read as a weakening of the inherited filter. Comparing somatic variants from 8,886 tumours with population variation using a unified analytical framework and a dataset-specific mutational null, we show that the tumour filter has a different shape. ATP synthase, the least constrained complex in the germline, becomes the most constrained in tumours, an inversion that holds within the tumour data alone and is not explained by the measurement ceiling. Holding residue position fixed, the germline avoids substitutions that change side-chain charge at the proton-loading sites of complex I, as does the human phylogeny, and around the haems of complex III, whereas tumours no longer distinguish them. Damage at the redox centres of complexes III and IV is tolerated mainly at low variant allele fraction, including within single cohorts, and tumours retain constraint on the electron-tunnelling medium of complex IV. At a complex I proton bridge, density-functional calculations separate substitutions that retune the transfer potential from those that abolish it, and a gated-tunnelling model predicts that removing the charge of one tumour-mutated residue changes the rate far more than the kinetic isotope effect.

items.title: Population-level learning of non-additive effects enables accurate and efficient prediction of combinatorial perturbation responses
items.corresponding_institution: Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard
items.abstract: Combinatorial perturbations are widely used to study genetic interactions and to develop drug combinations, but the number of possible combinations grows quadratically with the number of perturbations, and only a small fraction can be measured in a screen experiment. Despite their growing sophistication, deep-learning and foundation models often fail to outperform a simple additive baseline based on measured single-perturbation responses. This suggests a simpler approach that builds on these measurements and directly learns deviations from additivity at the population level. We therefore developed GAIN, a lightweight model that implements these principles by predicting the pseudobulk response to a combination as the sum of its two single-perturbation responses and a learned interaction term. Across three single-cell datasets of genetic and drug combinations, GAIN corrected deviations from additivity and outperformed the additive model and cell-level methods across generalization settings and metrics, while training 3- to 64-fold faster. Applied to a combinatorial CRISPR screen of leukemia differentiation regulators, GAIN revealed synergy between key regulators of the differentiation block and genes that restrain differentiation but have little effect alone. It also revealed dampening by the histone chaperone FACT, which supports the induction of differentiation genes. These results establish population-level modeling of the deviation from additivity as a simple, accurate and scalable approach to predicting combination responses.

items.title: Earl Grey ParTEA: scalable, consistent transposable element annotation from pangenomes to deep phylogenetic scopes
items.abstract: Transposable elements (TEs) are major drivers of genomic diversity, yet understanding their mobility and functional impact requires their accurate description in genomes. TE annotation is still typically performed genome-by-genome. TEs are often shared between some members of the same or closely related species. Hence, TE annotation with a library from a single reference misses families absent from that assembly, whereas building independent per-genome libraries fails to consistently surface shared TEs, hindering comparison. Here, we present Earl Grey ParTEA, a fully automated Snakemake pipeline extending the functionality of Earl Grey for comparative TE annotation across genome panels. ParTEA builds a single non-redundant TE library from all input genomes, resolves chimeric consensus sequences, and uses this shared library to annotate every genome, enabling direct comparison of TE family diversity, abundance, shared and private content, and activity landscapes. Optional modules provide TE library saturation analysis, BUSCO-based assembly quality control, and phylogenetic ordering of outputs. We applied ParTEA to sets of genomes spanning evolutionary scales: ten Arabidopsis thaliana accessions, ten Drosophila species, and ten species spanning the fungal kingdom. The Drosophila TE library expanded from 343 to 1,852 curated families including a previously missed rolling circle element with over 6,000 copies in D. miranda. The proportion of TE families shared across all genomes was highest within A. thaliana (97.3%), 37.7% across Drosophila species and only 0.5% across the set of fungi. ParTEA is available through Bioconda and represents a computationally efficient reproducible framework for comparative TE analysis in the era of large-scale genome analyses.

items.title: A2Holo: Dual-Stream Flow Matching of 3D Structure and a Protein Language Model for Conformational Transition Prediction
items.abstract: Modelling a ligand-bound holo conformation from a ligand-free apo conformation is essential in structure-based drug discovery. We present A2Holo, which casts apo-to-holo prediction as flow matching between two experimental structures rather than generation from noise. It transplants the dual-stream joint attention of in-context image generation to residue-aligned protein language model embeddings and structure. Without ligand conditioning or stochastic sampling, A2Holo's single deterministic trajectory reaches a median C RMSD of 0.809 [A] on the D3PM benchmark, the lowest among existing methods. Its TM-score exceeds even the best of 10 samples from every stochastic baseline on at least 144 of 150 pairs. Beyond performance, we directly measure the transplanted multimodal mechanism itself. Because sequence and structure are residue-aligned, its joint attention can be measured at residue resolution and tested for reproducibility across independently trained model variants. Within the structure stream, the attention a residue receives recovers moving residues better than the attention it emits, and this asymmetry is learned. A2Holo demonstrates a successful multimodal transplant from in-context image generation to protein conformational change, with strong deterministic apo-to-holo prediction. It also provides a quantitative account of how that mechanism organises residue-aligned sequence and structure around the residues that move.

items.title: siGMA: Modeling Label Noise and Heterogeneity in siRNA Efficacy Prediction
items.abstract: Small interfering RNAs (siRNAs) have emerged as a powerful class of therapeutics, yet identifying viable candidates remains costly and labour-intensive given the vast combination space that must be screened. This challenge is compounded by the need for chemical modifications, which are essential to mitigate off-target effects and enhance serum stability but frequently come at the expense of baseline knockdown efficacy. As a result, siRNA design requires careful, iterative optimization, further expanding the experimental burden and rendering exhaustive screening impractical. Computational prediction offers a compelling alternative, enabling rapid, low-cost identification of promising candidates prior to wet-lab validation. In this work we present siGMA, a heteroscedastic multimodal predictive model that integrates sequence, chemical, structural, and experimental information to predict the silencing efficacy of chemically modified siRNAs. Modelling in this domain is constrained by two principal obstacles: the scarcity of experimental data and the substantial noise arising from protocol heterogeneity across publicly available datasets. We therefore propose a model that quantifies predictive uncertainty rather than issuing confident mispredictions. We calibrated the model against such noise using a combined aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty prediction. The resulting model yielded well-calibrated estimates of predictive variability on held-out folds across datasets and outperformed current state-of-the-art approaches across noisy cross-dataset conditions, including previously unseen chemical modifications and target sequences. This demonstrates our model's ability to rank better than the baselines while rendering the noise ceiling measurable. This provides a scalable framework that could accelerate the therapeutic siRNA development pipeline while reducing the need for exhaustive empirical screening.

items.title: Dependence-Aware Conformal Prediction for 3D Uncertainty Quantification in Molecular Docking
items.abstract: Molecular docking plays a critical role in drug discovery by predicting three-dimensional (3D) binding poses of small molecules within proteins. However, docking predictions can contain substantial positional errors, making reliable uncertainty quantification essential. Conformal prediction (CP) provides a principled framework for uncertainty quantification, yet constructing compact 3D prediction regions with reliable joint coverage remains challenging due to heterogeneous atomic errors, dependence among spatial coordinates, and distribution shifts. We develop a dependence-aware CP framework for molecular docking that leverages a shared graph neural network (GNN) to estimate adaptive, asymmetric uncertainty intervals using local atomic and global molecular information. Copula-based joint calibration accounts for dependence among coordinate-wise nonconformity scores to construct compact 3D prediction boxes. We further introduce density ratio estimation (DRE) to adapt calibration under distribution shift. Experiments across three docking methods demonstrate that our approach reduces median prediction-box volumes by 37.40%, 95.00%, and 39.16% for AutoDock Vina, Protenix, and MedusaGraph, respectively, compared with a state-of-the-art CP baseline, while achieving empirical joint coverage close to the 90% target. Under the Molecular Group Split and controlled distribution shifts, DRE further reduces coverage deviations, highlighting the potential of dependence-aware and shift-adaptive calibration for reliable 3D molecular docking uncertainty quantification.

items.title: TSC/mTORC1-dependent proteostasis in stress-recruited prefrontal ensembles gates flexible avoidance
items.abstract: Adaptive threat responses require accurate appraisal of danger signals and flexible behavioral control. Anxiety and trauma-related disorders are marked by avoidance that outlasts the circumstances warranting it, yet such states rarely arise from genetic or environmental insult alone. Here we show that the two converge on a defined prefrontal population by releasing the TSC complex's constitutive brake on mTORC1. Using activity-dependent genetic targeting in mice, we accessed medial prefrontal cortex neurons recruited during the early phase of social isolation - a population projecting predominantly to the lateral septum - and deleted Tsc2 selectively within them. Ensemble-specific Tsc2 haploinsufficiency suppressed autophagic flux without altering bulk translation and produced behavioral avoidance that was rapid and efficient yet no longer under stimulus control, escalating into extra-CS epochs and generalizing to a novel, non-reinforced context. Mutant animals bypassed the phase in which freezing and shuttling compete, and in vivo calcium fiber photometry revealed ensembles locked to the cue but unable to signal trial outcome or track the competing Pavlovian response. Reinstating restraint on mTORC1 through ensemble-restricted Raptor knockdown or systemic Rapamycin restored stimulus control over avoidance, whereas Tsc2 haploinsufficiency in mPFC neurons without social isolation produced no phenotype. These findings identify TSC-restrained, mTORC1-dependent proteostasis within stress-recruited ensembles as a gene-by-environment locus for maladaptive avoidance. More broadly, they suggest that excessive avoidance in anxiety and post-traumatic stress disorders may arise not from genetic risk or adversity alone but from their convergence on mTORC1 signaling cascade.

items.title: Glial involvement in mitochondrial metabolic alterations in Alzheimer's disease
items.corresponding_institution: Institute for Quantum Life Science, National Institutes for Quantum Science and Technology, Chiba, Japan
items.abstract: Metabolic alterations in the posterior cingulate cortex (PCC) emerge early in Alzheimer's disease (AD), but their molecular and cellular basis remains unclear. We hypothesized that impaired glial energy metabolism, particularly mitochondrial oxidative metabolism in astrocytes, underlies the metabolic vulnerability of the PCC in AD. To test this hypothesis, we integrated human PCC proteomics and transcriptomics with magnetic resonance spectroscopy in AppNL-G-F knock-in (APP-KI) mice. Human proteomic and transcriptomic analyses converged on reduced mitochondrial oxidative-metabolism signatures associated with AD pathology and cognition. APP-KI hippocampus showed proteomic and 1H-MRS alterations resembling those in the human AD PCC. Spatial transcriptomics identified widespread metabolic transcriptional changes and reduced mitochondrial pathway signatures in glia-enriched hippocampal clusters. Hyperpolarized [1-13C]pyruvate spectroscopy showed reduced bicarbonate labelling in APP-KI mice, consistent with impaired oxidative pyruvate metabolism. These findings reveal convergent mitochondrial alterations in human AD and APP-KI mice, implicating glial cells, particularly astrocytes, in the associated dysfunction.

items.title: Cross- species developmental multiomics identifies RHOJ as a regulator of human-enriched cortical progenitor states
items.abstract: Expansion of the primate cerebral cortex is associated with increased proliferation and diversification of neural progenitors, particularly outer radial glia (oRG), but the evolutionary developmental changes underlying these features remain unclear. Here, we integrate time-resolved, paired single-nucleus transcriptomic and chromatin-accessibility profiles from human, macaque and mouse fetal cortex to compare their radial glial developmental programs. Developmental alignment within a conserved corticogenic framework identified two human-enriched programs associated with oRG features and progenitor maintenance. We identified RHOJ, which encodes a conserved small GTPase, as an oRG-enriched gene with elevated expression in human cortex. Ectopic RHOJ expression in mouse fetal cortex increased the proportions of neural progenitors and cells with oRG-like morphology, and altered the relative abundance of SATB2+ and TBR1+ neuronal populations. An intronic RHOJ enhancer showed greater reporter activity for the human sequence than for orthologous non-human primate sequences, partly attributable to a human-specific substitution within a predicted AP-1 binding motif. In human cortical organoids, deletion of this enhancer reduced RHOJ expression, impaired organoid growth and altered progenitor and neuronal populations. These findings link human-enriched developmental programs to evolutionary modification of progenitor properties, supporting altered deployment of conserved genes as a potential contributor to cortical progenitor diversification.

items.title: RhoA Overexpression in Nucleus Accumbens-to-Ventral Tegmental Area Spiny Projection Neurons Induces Negative Affective-like Behavior
items.corresponding_institution: Department of Neurobiology, University of Maryland School of Medicine, Baltimore, Maryland, USA.
items.abstract: Rationale. Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) is increasingly affecting populations worldwide and becoming a leading cause of psychological disabilities. However, MDD patients do not respond to current medications, resulting in treatment resistance. This situation demands more basic research to identify targetable molecules and the specific brain circuits and cell types that underlie negative affective pathology. Ras homolog family member A (RhoA) mediates negative affective-like behaviors via dendritic atrophy of nucleus accumbens (NAc) D1 (dopamine receptor 1)-Spiny Projection Neurons (SPNs), making RhoA a promising target for new depression therapeutics. However, the sufficiency of RhoA elevation in NAc projection-specific D1-SPNs is yet to be investigated. Objectives. Whether RhoA overexpression selectively in NAc-to-ventral tegmental area (VTA) SPNs (NAc-VTA SPNs) is sufficient to induce negative affective-like behavior. Whether chronic stress (CS) induces RhoA mRNA expression in this specific projection. Methods. A retrograde (Rg) vector expressing Cre recombinase was infused into the VTA together with Cre-dependent vectors overexpressing either a control expressing only enhanced Yellow Fluorescent Protein (eYFP) or RhoA-eYFP in NAc-VTA neurons. Mice then underwent a battery of affective assays (social interaction, etc.) and a two-choice sucrose operant task assessing motivation. RNA in situ hybridization (RHA-ish) quantified RhoA mRNA in NAc-VTA D1-SPNs of chronically stressed versus unstressed (control) mice. Results. RhoA overexpression in NAc-VTA SPNs, which are primarily D1-SPNs, elicited negative affective-like phenotypes, including social avoidance, reduced open-arm exploration, decreased grooming, and increased latency to approach food. RhoA and control groups acquired a food operant task similarly. However, RhoA overexpression significantly reduced operant responding and breakpoint during progressive-ratio testing. RhoA overexpression in the NAc-VTA projection neurons also diminished persistent sucrose-seeking behavior. Chronic stress induced RhoA mRNA expression selectively in NAc-VTA neurons.

items.title: SCOPE: Gaussian-regularized graph learning for enzyme catalytic residue prediction
items.abstract: Accurate identification of catalytic residues is central to understanding enzyme mechanisms and engineering biocatalysts, yet annotation remains challenging because experimentally validated sites are sparse. Here, we present SCOPE, a graph learning framework for catalytic residue prediction that integrates evolutionary, physicochemical, and three-dimensional structural information at the residue level. SCOPE represents enzymes as residue-level structural graphs and incorporates a Gaussian auxiliary training objective that aggregates structure-aware representations along sequence order. Evaluations across five benchmark datasets, CATH family-disjoint retraining and the external CataloDB benchmark assess predictive performance and generalization. Structural analyses associate complete catalytic-residue recovery with compact active-site arrangements. We further validated SCOPE prospectively across four enzymes using site-directed mutagenesis and activity assays, confirming multiple predicted residues as functionally important. These results support SCOPE as a framework for catalytic residue annotation and prioritizing functional sites for experimental investigation.

items.title: gutenTAG: A MALDI-IHC processing and quality control tool
items.abstract: Coupling of immunohistochemistry with MALDI mass spectroscopy (MALDI-IHC) enables targeted spatial analysis of proteins through the use of photocleavable mass tags. Upwards of 100 proteins can be imaged in a single run due to the high multiplexing power of this technology. Coupled with mass shifts in MALDI-IHC data, this scalability creates a challenge for users, as there are currently no dedicated software tools for MALDI-IHC data processing. Here we introduce gutenTAG, an open-source processing and quality control tool specifically designed for MALDI-IHC. gutenTAG uses a novel strategy based on grouping clusters of m/z bins originating from the same molecular species into single entities termed metapeaks. This strategy is robust to mass shift, generating ion images that capture the full signal of peaks corresponding to each mass tag while minimizing noise. Furthermore, we show that the metapeak strategy can be adapted to alternative open-source tools to facilitate their use in targeted imaging applications.

items.title: SpliceVarMech: A causal generative framework for mechanistic interpretation of non-canonical splicing variants
items.abstract: Non-canonical splicing variants occur beyond the conserved dinucleotides flanking splice junctions and are difficult to interpret because disruption scores alone do not explain splice outcomes or quantify uncertainty. We have developed SpliceVarMech, a causal generative framework in which a dual-stream encoder compares the wild-type and mutant sequences and conditional discrete sequence diffusion generates candidate splice outcomes. We then apply Bayesian causal inference to estimate posterior disruption probabilities with 95% credible intervals. The framework reports the predicted splice mechanism together with sequence attribution maps and an exploratory mapping to clinical evidence labels. On a gold-standard cohort of experimentally validated variants from male infertility genes, Bayesian leave-one-out cross-validation on 31 variants yielded an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 1.000. We benchmarked 16 individual splice prediction tools on the same cohort, where the highest-performing tool, SpliceAI, achieved 0.619 on its 30 scored variants.
